Ligand 1 has the highest QED in the pool (0.910) but its SA is 2.80, which alone caps Phi near 1.71 however active I make it, and its stereocentre at atom 5 is an anchor I must avoid. So I will harvest its useful piece - the 1,2-disubstituted fluoroaryl - and discard the sulfonamido-lactam. Step 1 installs the azine link in place of the chlorine: atom 12 is the aromatic carbon bearing Cl at atom 13, a non-ring bond, so I swap the halogen for an N-linked pyridin-2-ylamino. Choosing pyridine rather than pyrimidine here is deliberate: every link I have installed so far has been a 1,3-diazine, so I cannot yet tell whether the model wants two ring nitrogens or just one electron-poor N ortho to the NH. A 2-aminopyridine link answers that, and it costs one fewer nitrogen of TPSA.

QED is holding well at 0.841, but SA is still 2.873 and that is now the binding constraint - the sulfonamido-lactam with its stereocentre is what makes this molecule hard to make, and it contributes no NH-azine linkage of its own (the lactam nitrogen at atom 8 is tertiary, and the sulfonamide NH is aliphatic). Atom 9 is the aromatic carbon attached to that lactam nitrogen and the 9-8 bond is non-ring, so cutting it discards the entire pyrrolidinone and sulfonamide - eleven atoms - and I attach an N-linked acetamido in their place. The result is N-[3-fluoro-4-(pyridin-2-ylamino)phenyl]acetamide at ~245 Da: two aryl-NH links, no stereocentre, SA should fall under 2, TPSA near 67, LogP near 1.9. Small, flat, cheap and carrying the pyridine-versus-pyrimidine comparison I set up.
